tasks.task: Locate and use the compose email feature to draft a new email.
tasks.expected: The platform displays a new email composition interface with fields for the subject, body, recipients, and attachment options.

tasks.task: Select a recipient from the recipient management list and add them to the new email.
tasks.expected: The selected recipient is added to the recipients' field in the compose email interface.

tasks.task: Upload an attachment to an email draft.
tasks.expected: The attachment is successfully uploaded and displayed within the email draft without any errors.

tasks.task: Send a composed email to the selected recipients.
tasks.expected: The email is successfully sent, a confirmation message is received, and the email appears in the sent emails folder.

tasks.task: Access the sent emails section and verify that the recently sent email is present.
tasks.expected: The sent emails section displays the recently sent email with the correct recipient and timestamp.

tasks.task: Create and save a new email template.
tasks.expected: The email template is saved successfully and available for future use in the templates section.

tasks.task: Edit an existing email template and save the changes.
tasks.expected: The edited template is updated correctly and displayed with the changes in the templates section.

tasks.task: Verify that the website uses 'cornsilk' as the background color and 'peru' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
tasks.expected: The website has a background color of 'cornsilk' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'peru', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

tasks.task: On the Delivery Log page, choose the delivered status filter and type acme into the search box.
tasks.expected: Exactly 3 rows remain — gus@acme.com, ana@acme.com, and ben@acme.com, newest first — with the bounced and failed entries gone.

tasks.task: Open the Delivery Log page fresh.
tasks.expected: All seven seeded entries are shown newest first — gus@acme.com's Jan 9 email at the top and dev@nova.io's Jan 3 email at the bottom — each with a colored status badge.

tasks.task: Type zzz into the Delivery Log's search box, then clear it.
tasks.expected: While zzz is entered, a friendly no-results state shows with zero rows (no crash or blank screen); clearing the search brings back all seven rows.

tasks.task: From compose, send an email to ana@acme.com with subject Checking in, then open the Delivery Log.
tasks.expected: A new row for ana@acme.com with subject Checking in sits at the top of the log with a green delivered badge and 0 opens, making eight entries total.

tasks.task: Compose an email with recipient test@example.com and subject Hello, send it, then open the sent emails area.
tasks.expected: The Hello email to test@example.com appears among the sent emails.

tasks.task: On the Blocklist page, type not-an-email into the add-address field and try to add it.
tasks.expected: An invalid-format indication appears while the text is being entered, and the address is not added — the list still shows only its two entries.

tasks.task: Type CARA@NOVA.IO into the blocklist add field and try to add it.
tasks.expected: It is rejected as a duplicate of cara@nova.io (case-insensitive match), the list still has exactly two entries, and both display in lowercase.

tasks.task: Add eli@orbit.dev to the blocklist.
tasks.expected: The list shows exactly three entries in alphabetical order: cara@nova.io, eli@orbit.dev, spam-trap@bait.org.

tasks.task: In compose, set the recipient to cara@nova.io, enter any subject, and hit send.
tasks.expected: The send is stopped with an inline warning naming cara@nova.io as blocked, and no new email appears in the sent emails area.

tasks.task: On the Delivery Log page, choose the delivered status filter and type acme into the search box.
tasks.expected: Exactly 3 rows remain — gus@acme.com, ana@acme.com, and ben@acme.com, newest first — with the bounced and failed entries gone.

tasks.task: Open the Analytics page and check the open rate.
tasks.expected: The open rate reads 80.0% — 4 of the 5 delivered emails were opened at least once; a value like 57.1% would mean bounced and failed emails were wrongly counted in the denominator.

tasks.task: Look at the top-recipients-by-opens leaderboard on the Analytics page.
tasks.expected: ana@acme.com ranks above dev@nova.io — both have 3 opens and the tie is broken alphabetically by address, not by which email came first.

tasks.task: Check the bounce rate and the status breakdown on the Analytics page.
tasks.expected: The bounce rate reads 14.3%, and the breakdown shows delivered 5, bounced 1, failed 1 — summing to the 7 total.

tasks.task: Send a fresh email from compose to ben@acme.com with subject Ping, then open the Analytics page.
tasks.expected: Total emails becomes 8 and the open rate drops to 66.7% — 4 opened out of 6 delivered — showing the stats recomputed from the updated log.

tasks.task: Open the Delivery Log page fresh.
tasks.expected: All seven seeded entries are shown newest first — gus@acme.com's Jan 9 email at the top and dev@nova.io's Jan 3 email at the bottom — each with a colored status badge.

tasks.task: Open the Outbox page.
tasks.expected: The frozen clock Jan 10, 2025, 9:00 AM is shown, and the three queued emails read top to bottom: fay@orbit.dev (Jan 11 3:00 PM), then ben@acme.com, then gus@acme.com — the two Jan 12 10:00 AM items are tie-broken alphabetically, not listed in the order they were added.

tasks.task: In compose, choose schedule-for-later for an email to ana@acme.com, type Jan 9, 2025 8:00 AM as the time, and confirm.
tasks.expected: It is rejected with a visible error because the time isn't after the frozen Jan 10, 2025 9:00 AM clock, and the Outbox still holds exactly three items.

tasks.task: From compose, schedule an email with subject Sync up to ana@acme.com for Jan 11, 2025 9:00 AM, then open the Outbox.
tasks.expected: The new item appears first in the queue, above fay@orbit.dev's Jan 11 3:00 PM email.

tasks.task: Click Send now on fay@orbit.dev's queued email, then open the Delivery Log.
tasks.expected: The 'Quarterly review' email is gone from the Outbox and sits at the top of the Delivery Log with a green delivered badge and 0 opens.

tasks.task: On the Blocklist page, type not-an-email into the add-address field and try to add it.
tasks.expected: An invalid-format indication appears while the text is being entered, and the address is not added — the list still shows only its two entries.

tasks.task: In compose, type 'Hi {{first_name}}, welcome {{first_name}}!' into the body and type Ana into the preview's first-name field.
tasks.expected: The preview updates as the text is typed and reads 'Hi Ana, welcome Ana!' — both occurrences replaced, not just the first.

tasks.task: Type 'Hi {{first_name}}' into the body, then pick cara@nova.io as the sample recipient from the delivery-log people.
tasks.expected: The first-name field prefills to Cara and the preview reads 'Hi Cara'.

tasks.task: Type '{{firstname}} and {{company}}' into the body and type Acme into the preview's company field.
tasks.expected: The preview shows Acme substituted for {{company}}, leaves {{firstname}} visible and flagged as unrecognized, and the unresolved-placeholder count reads 1.

tasks.task: Type ANA@ACME.COM into the preview's sample recipient email field.
tasks.expected: The preview's To: line shows the address lowercased as ana@acme.com.

tasks.task: Open the Analytics page and check the open rate.
tasks.expected: The open rate reads 80.0% — 4 of the 5 delivered emails were opened at least once; a value like 57.1% would mean bounced and failed emails were wrongly counted in the denominator.

tasks.task: Open the A/B results view for the seeded 'Spring sale starts now' vs 'Sale ends soon' test.
tasks.expected: Variant A is the winner with a 27.5% open rate against B's 26.7% — even though B had more raw opens (16 vs 11).

tasks.task: In the A/B setup, type 95 into the split percentage field and try to continue.
tasks.expected: It is rejected with a validation message (only whole numbers 10 through 90 are allowed) and the flow does not advance to review.

tasks.task: Set up a test with subject A 'Hello A', subject B 'Hello B', split 30, and continue to the review step.
tasks.expected: The review shows an audience of 6 (cara@nova.io is excluded via the blocklist), with 1 recipient going to variant A — ana@acme.com, alphabetically first, since 30% of 6 rounds down from 1.8 — and 5 going to B.

tasks.task: Set up an A/B test with subject A 'Hello A', subject B 'Hello B', split 30, launch it from the review step, then open the Delivery Log.
tasks.expected: Exactly six new entries appear — none for the blocklisted cara@nova.io — and dev@nova.io's new entry carries the 'Hello B' subject.

tasks.task: Open the Outbox page.
tasks.expected: The frozen clock Jan 10, 2025, 9:00 AM is shown, and the three queued emails read top to bottom: fay@orbit.dev (Jan 11 3:00 PM), then ben@acme.com, then gus@acme.com — the two Jan 12 10:00 AM items are tie-broken alphabetically, not listed in the order they were added.

tasks.task: Open the saved 'Nova fans' segment.
tasks.expected: It has exactly one member, dev@nova.io — cara@nova.io matches the nova.io domain but is left out because she is blocklisted, so the count reads 1, not 2.

tasks.task: In the segment builder, set the domain filter to acme.com and turn on the opened-at-least-once engagement filter.
tasks.expected: The live member list narrows to exactly ana@acme.com and gus@acme.com — ben@acme.com drops out with 0 opens — and the member count matches the list at 2.

tasks.task: Set the segment builder's domain filter to legacy.net.
tasks.expected: The member count reads 0 with a clear empty message instead of a blank or crash, and saving the segment is prevented.

tasks.task: In compose, pick the saved 'Nova fans' segment to fill in the recipients.
tasks.expected: The recipient field is populated with only dev@nova.io.

tasks.task: Type 'Hi {{first_name}}' into the body, then pick cara@nova.io as the sample recipient from the delivery-log people.
tasks.expected: The first-name field prefills to Cara and the preview reads 'Hi Cara'.

tasks.task: Open the Blocklist page and look at the add button and the page title.
tasks.expected: The add button is deep forest green (#2D6A4F) with white text, and the page title is centered.

tasks.task: Open the Delivery Log and find cara@nova.io's row.
tasks.expected: Her status is a pill-shaped amber badge reading 'Bounced' with a capital B.

tasks.task: Visit the Analytics page and then the Outbox page.
tasks.expected: Both pages show the same shared top nav linking to all sections, both page titles are centered, and cards on each page have rounded corners — no page is left on the old style.

tasks.task: On the restyled Analytics page, read the open rate figure.
tasks.expected: It still shows exactly one decimal place — 80.0% — the restyle didn't break the percentage formatting.
